podcast.title: Still no flying cars

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: When you were a child, what did you think the future would look like? Guess: what did ten-year-old Sam predict for 2025?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is the future. And I found something funny at my parents' house — a letter I wrote when I was ten, called "The world in 2025".
[laugh] Oh no. What were your predictions?
Flying cars, robot teachers and holidays on the Moon. My only correct prediction was that phones would get smaller. And then they got bigger again!
Well, nobody has a crystal ball. Even the weather forecast is wrong half the time.
True. But some things changed faster than anyone thought. When I was ten, nobody had a smartphone.
And now my grandmother sends me voice messages every morning! She's eighty.
That's brilliant. So there's no generation gap in your family?
[laugh] Oh, there is. She still thinks my job isn't a real job, because I work on a laptop at home.
Ha! And in ten years, our things will be obsolete too. Our grandchildren will laugh at our phones.
Like we laugh at CDs. What innovation do you think is coming next?
I think AI will change a lot of jobs. That kind of disruption can be scary — some jobs will disappear, but new ones will appear too.
I hope people stay in control. Technology is only a tool. People shape the future, not machines.
Well said. What about the planet? Are you optimistic?
Half and half. We need a more sustainable way to live — cleaner energy, less waste. I think more electric cars in Baku is only a matter of time.
In Manchester there are already a lot. And bikes everywhere.
What would your perfect future look like? Your utopia?
Hmm. Short working weeks, clean air, and trains that are never late.
[laugh] Trains that are never late? Now that's science fiction.
Let me dream! What about yours?
A world where anyone can talk to anyone and really understand each other. Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is one prediction you have for the world in twenty years?
Mine: still no flying cars. See you next time!
Bye for now!
